clue.text: Theologian with duty to provide daily service

parts.note: a divine is a clergyman or student of theology
an office is a duty or function one performs

explanation.surface: A churchman is told it is part of his job to lead a service every day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Divine Office is the cycle of daily prayer services said by clergy, especially in the Catholic and Anglican traditions.
explanation.definitionFit: The liturgical hours of prayer said each day by clergy are known by this name.

clue.text: Demand payment from church in France

parts.note: to dun someone is to press them for a debt
kirk is the Scottish word for a church

explanation.surface: A creditor chases money owed by a French parish church.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the slim 'in France': the answer is a port on the French coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a northern French port town, so it is a place found in that country.

clue.text: Foreign tourist hid it in face-mask

indicators.note: hid, with in, means one piece has been tucked away inside another
in tells us where the word it is placed: inside the mask

parts.note: a visor is a shield or mask covering the face

explanation.surface: An overseas tourist conceals something behind a face covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor is someone who comes from elsewhere, as a foreign tourist does.

clue.text: Am insured to work with children!

definitions.text: Am insured to work with children!

indicators.note: to work suggests the letters being worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A carer exclaims that she has insurance for her job looking after youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of AM INSURED rearrange to give the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny employed to care for young ones is exactly someone who works with kids.

clue.text: Chose to get work with lord Wilson's successor

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
Harold Wilson, later Lord Wilson, was succeeded as Labour's opponent in Downing Street by Edward 'Ted' Heath in 1970

explanation.surface: Someone elects to take a job under the man who followed a former prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath was the British prime minister who followed Harold Wilson in 1970; Wilson was later made a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: To have opted is to have picked or decided on something.

clue.text: Female not just offering family entertainment

parts.note: something not just is unfair

explanation.surface: A woman complains that something is unfair while laying on a show for families.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground with rides and stalls is a classic outing for parents and kids.

clue.text: New rector embraces fellow farmer

indicators.note: embraces means the rearranged word holds another piece inside it
new suggests the letters being made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A newly arrived vicar hugs a man who works the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' turns RECTOR into CROTER, and 'embraces' puts F inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A crofter works a small rented holding in the Scottish Highlands, a smallholder.

clue.text: Concert performer has to understand what's what

definitions.meaning: a musician playing in an orchestra must be familiar with the written music
an idiom for being aware of the real state of affairs

explanation.surface: A musician on stage must grasp how things really stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a player must learn the printed music; idiomatically the phrase means being well informed about a situation.

clue.text: No French employer ignores rights

definitions.note: a noun phrase in the answer, someone or something failing to exercise a right

parts.note: non is French for no
an employer of something is one who uses it

explanation.surface: A French boss refuses to respect workers' entitlements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employer' looks like a boss, but here it means one who employs, i.e. uses, a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, failing to exercise a right one holds, so that it may lapse, is termed this.

clue.text: Oven with light-brown aperture

parts.note: tan is a light yellowish-brown colour
a door is an opening or entrance

explanation.surface: A cooker is described by its colour and its opening.
explanation.walkthrough: A tandoor is the clay oven of Indian cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A cylindrical clay oven used in Indian and Punjabi cooking.

clue.text: Summarise details concerning surrender

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to capitulate is to give in

explanation.surface: Someone gives a summary of the terms of a surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to go over the main points again briefly.

clue.text: Sound cheerful when going around street

indicators.note: going around means one word encloses the other

parts.note: while means during the time that, as when does

explanation.surface: Someone sounds happy as they stroll round the block.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing a tune through pursed lips is a classic sign of being in good spirits.

clue.text: Severe physician with a small neuralgic complaint

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
tic douloureux is a facial neuralgia, a tic for short

explanation.surface: A doctor with a minor nerve problem is described as harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are extreme or harsh ones.

clue.text: Footman took Eisenhower into house of representatives

indicators.note: into means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: HR is the abbreviation for the US House of Representatives
Ike was the nickname of US president Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A servant escorts the US president into Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Footman' looks like a servant but means someone travelling on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler going on foot is literally a man of the feet.

clue.text: A poor 6 quietly reaps another harvest

indicators.note: poor suggests that answer being battered into a new order

parts.note: 6 refers to the answer at 6 down, a smallholding farmer
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A struggling smallholder quietly brings in a second crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges the letters of the 6-down answer to give FTERCRO, between A and P.
explanation.definitionFit: A second crop grown in the same season after the main one is this.

clue.text: Witnessing examination by articulate Asian

parts.note: a test is an examination

indicators.note: articulate means said out loud, so the next word is heard rather than written

parts.note: the word Asian is pronounced like the ending ation

explanation.surface: An Asian student sits an exam while observers look on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articulate' looks like an adjective but is a verb: say 'Asian' and it sounds like ATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Testation is the act of bearing witness or attesting.

clue.text: Better risk looking weird in lederhosen!

definitions.meaning: a punter, or better, prefers a bet whose odds suggest a likely winner
lederhosen are leather shorts, so someone wearing them looks odd in shorts

explanation.surface: A gambler weighs the chances of looking silly in Bavarian leather trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is one who bets. Lederhosen are short leather trousers worn in Bavaria.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, a low payout reflects a high chance of winning, a safer wager; read playfully it describes someone odd in shorts.

clue.text: Former head of English entered punctually

indicators.note: entered means the letter has gone inside the other phrase

parts.note: arriving punctually means arriving on time

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The former head of the English department arrived exactly on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Onetime means previous or erstwhile, as in a onetime champion.

clue.text: Consequently ambassador went in to negotiate

indicators.note: went in means one piece has been put inside the other

parts.note: to treat is to negotiate terms
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: As a result, the envoy entered to conduct talks.
explanation.walkthrough: HE (His Excellency) is the usual way of addressing an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereat is an archaic word meaning because of that, or as a result.

clue.text: Could possibly gain power

definitions.meaning: strength or force, as in with all one's strength

explanation.surface: Someone may be able to seize control.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as a past modal of possibility and as a noun for strength or force.

clue.text: Signals pioneer from Minorca

indicators.note: from indicates that the answer is fashioned out of the letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A trailblazer in communications hails from a Spanish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Guglielmo Marconi pioneered long-distance radio telegraphy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian inventor developed wireless telegraphy, sending radio signals across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Burning finally, laying waste and consuming grass

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: razing means demolishing or laying waste

explanation.surface: Fire, then destruction, then animals eating the pasture.
explanation.definitionFit: Livestock feeding on growing pasture are said to be doing this.

clue.text: No peers ordered starters

indicators.note: ordered suggests the letters being arranged anew

explanation.surface: Without any lords present, the first courses are requested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like requesting food at a meal but signals rearranging NO PEERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Openers are things that begin something, such as first courses or opening batsmen.

clue.text: Reeked of fish

definitions.meaning: gave off a strong odour, a past tense in British use
a small silvery fish of the salmon family

explanation.surface: Something stank of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a British past tense of a verb meaning to stink, and also the name of a small edible fish.

clue.text: Top-flight post gives top-rate marines trouble

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
RM is the abbreviation for the Royal Marines
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: First-class mail sent by plane annoys the marines.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate) appears as AI; 'Top-flight' refers to letters carried high up by plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters carried by aeroplane travel at altitude, a playful sense of top-flight.

clue.text: Curse English village, I hear

indicators.note: hear tells us the preceding words are spoken out loud rather than written

parts.note: E for English, then VILL, an old word for a village, then I: said together they make EVILLI

explanation.surface: Someone claims an English village has been put under a hex.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, E-VILL-I sounds like the two-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A malevolent stare believed to bring harm or bad luck is a kind of hex.

clue.text: Club first joined by sarcastic master

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
1st, with the figure 1 read as the letter I, gives IST

explanation.surface: A golf club owner teams up with a mocking expert.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure 1 in 1ST is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled in mockery and saying the opposite of what they mean is an expert in irony.

clue.text: Socialists seeking election are roundly defeated

definitions.meaning: left-wing candidates putting themselves forward for office
being abandoned or outpaced completely by rivals

explanation.surface: Left-wing candidates take a heavy beating at the polls.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally it describes left-wingers running for office; idiomatically it means being outclassed by competitors.
